_schema: Fidelity-gap lookup for the Analog Portfolio Fidelity Gap panel (plan.md §2.4). Top-level 'tiers' has three keys: 'never_on_earth' (condition does not occur at any natural Earth site; never scored, shown as a constant panel), 'beyond_earth_range' (Earth has the direction but not the magnitude; scored against the Earth-clipped target t*, residual shown), 'coverable' (Earth sites can match within range; normal set cover, optional lab augmentation). Each tier has 'description' and 'gaps' (list). Each gap: id (snake_case), label (UI text), factors (plan.md factor IDs F1–F13 it affects; 'not_scored' if it is outside the scored factors), values (moon/mars/earth with unit and source_urls; 'derived' notes our own arithmetic; null where not found), facility_types (generic), example_facilities (keys into top-level 'facilities'), handling (how the engine/UI treats it), citation_urls, optional note. 'facilities' maps id -> {name, type, operator, location, provides, url[, url_alt]}. Facility capability numbers are quoted from the linked page. Compiled 2026-10-08 IST by Researcher; on that date every non-DOI URL returned HTTP 200 to curl, and every DOI (doi.org / science.org) was confirmed to exist via the Crossref API (publishers often block automated fetches).

never_on_earth.description: Conditions no natural Earth site provides. Not scored; shown with absolute numbers and the facility type that fills the gap.

gaps.label: Reduced gravity (1/6 g Moon, ~3/8 g Mars)
gaps.handling: Constant panel. Affects regolith mechanics, dust behaviour and EVA/mobility, which field analogs test only at 1 g.

gaps.label: Hard vacuum (Moon)
gaps.handling: Constant panel; F11 enters only as a capped tie-breaker.

gaps.label: Ionizing radiation dose (100–200× Earth background)
gaps.handling: F11 is log10 + directional within-Earth percentile × cap c (plan.md §2.4); absolute doses shown alongside.
gaps.note: Moon value: Chang'E-4 LND dose equivalent (far side). Mars value: MSL RAD at Gale, 0.64 ± 0.12 mSv/day.

gaps.label: Unfiltered solar UV (Mars ~10³× present Earth, DNA-weighted; Moon unshielded)

values.derived: Inferred: Cockell et al. 2000 put present Mars ≈ early (Archean) Earth and present Earth almost 3 orders of magnitude below Archean

gaps.note: No citable lunar surface UV dose number was used; Earth peak UVI reports of 43 (Cabrol 2014) are disputed (~25 ± 5 realistic).

gaps.label: Electrostatically charged, abrasive lunar dust
gaps.handling: Shown on Moon target cards; no Earth field site reproduces UV/plasma-driven dust charging.

gaps.label: Thin CO₂ atmosphere (95.1% CO₂)
gaps.handling: Not scored; relevant to dust/aeolian behaviour, ISRU chemistry and instrument testing.

beyond_earth_range.description: Earth varies in the right direction but cannot reach the target magnitude. Scored against t* = clip(t, Earth P0.5, Earth P99.5); the panel shows 'best Earth: X; target: Y; residual: Z'.

gaps.label: Lunar day–night temperature swing (~300 K)

values.moon: 95–390 K at equator (ΔT ≈ 298 K from Diviner max 392.3 / min 94.3 K)
values.earth: 283–293 K mean diurnal (NSSDC); Earth's maximum surface amplitude: not found as a citable value
values.derived: Moon ΔT 298 K and Mars ΔT 58 K are our subtraction

gaps.handling: Score vs t*; show residual. Mars ΔT is probably reachable in deserts (Earth max not verified), so Mars targets may fall in 'coverable'.

gaps.label: Permanently shadowed cold traps (<110 K; ~38 K at LCROSS site)
gaps.handling: F9 matches functionally (permafrost/ground ice) but F1 temperature cannot reach PSR values; residual shown.

gaps.label: South-polar ridge temperatures (~200 K in summer; colder in shadow)

values.moon: ~200 K summer on Connecting Ridge; ridge crests generally >~120 K

gaps.handling: Score vs t*; coldest Earth cells (Antarctic plateau) define t*.
gaps.note: No citable Earth minimum mean surface temperature was compiled here; it will come from the Earth layer (P0.5).

gaps.label: Near-horizon sun with long shadows and black sky (lunar south pole)

values.moon: best ridge points sunlit ~89–96% of the time with the Sun near the horizon

gaps.handling: Gaussian on sun elevation; high-latitude Earth summers give low sun but not airless contrast or year-round near-horizon geometry.
gaps.note: Partly coverable: Earth polar-day sites match low sun elevation seasonally.

coverable.description: Earth sites can match within range; handled by normal set cover. Lab facilities listed are optional augmentation.

gaps.label: Lander-safe slopes (Moon ≤8°, goal ≤5°; Starship <5° at 10 m)
gaps.handling: Fraction of area below threshold at a recorded baseline.

gaps.label: Local relief (ridges, massifs, crater rims)
gaps.handling: Ratio similarity on relief, never absolute elevation.

gaps.label: Basaltic (Mars, mare) and anorthositic (lunar highland) rock
gaps.handling: Similarity matrix; anorthosite is rare on Earth (e.g. Stillwater), so lunar-highland lithology may be thin in the portfolio.

gaps.label: Hyper-arid, barren, lifeless surface
gaps.handling: Directional within-Earth percentile (aridity) and bounded fraction (barrenness).

gaps.label: Ground ice / permafrost

values.mars: ice table 4.6 cm at Phoenix; SWIM depth bands 0–1, 1–5, >5 m

gaps.handling: Bounded fraction / depth-band match; Dry Valleys and Arctic permafrost are functional analogs.

gaps.label: Regolith thermophysical class (dusty ↔ rocky)
gaps.handling: Within-body percentile → 5 classes; Earth ATI is ordinal only (not TI units).

gaps.label: Mars mean surface temperature (~214 K)
gaps.handling: Polar/high-altitude Earth cells approach it; if Earth P0.5 > 214 K the residual is shown (moves to beyond_earth_range).
gaps.note: Earth-side extreme to be read from the F1 layer; not asserted here.

gaps.label: Impact craters, lava tubes/caves, periglacial terrain

novespace_air_zero_g.name: Novespace Air Zero G (A310 parabolic flights)
novespace_air_zero_g.provides: A310 weightless flights (public Air Zero G flights consist of 15 parabolas) plus scientific research flight campaigns; Novespace is a CNES subsidiary. Partial-gravity (Moon/Mars) parabola availability not confirmed on the linked page.

zarm_drop_tower.name: ZARM Bremen Drop Tower
zarm_drop_tower.provides: Up to 9.3 s of weightlessness (catapult mode).

zarm_gravitower.name: ZARM GraviTower Bremen Pro
zarm_gravitower.provides: High-cadence microgravity runs and partial-gravity runs 'as found on the Moon or Mars'.

nasa_grc_zero_g.name: NASA Glenn Zero Gravity Research Facility
nasa_grc_zero_g.provides: Near-weightless environment for 5.18 s in a vacuum drop shaft.

nasa_jsc_argos.name: NASA JSC Active Response Gravity Offload System (ARGOS)
nasa_jsc_argos.provides: Robotic overhead offload simulating lunar, Martian or micro-gravity for suited crew, rovers and robots.

nasa_grc_armstrong_sec.name: NASA Glenn Neil A. Armstrong Test Facility, Space Environments Complex (Space Simulation Vacuum Chamber, formerly Space Power Facility)
nasa_grc_armstrong_sec.provides: World's largest vacuum chamber: 30.5 m dia × 37.2 m high; vacuum < 4×10⁻⁶ Torr; cryoshroud −160 °C to +80 °C.

nasa_jsc_chamber_a.name: NASA JSC Chamber A (Space Environment Simulation Laboratory)
nasa_jsc_chamber_a.provides: Thermal-vacuum chamber with a 20 K helium-refrigerated shroud (commissioned for JWST cryo-vac testing).

bnl_nsrl.name: NASA Space Radiation Laboratory (NSRL) at Brookhaven National Laboratory
bnl_nsrl.provides: Accelerator beams of heavy ions and protons to study cosmic-radiation effects on biology and electronics.

dlr_paslab.name: DLR Planetary Analogue Simulation Laboratory (PASLAB)
dlr_paslab.provides: Three chambers simulating pressure, temperature, radiation, gas composition and humidity in diurnal cycles for present/early Mars.

dlr_mars_uv_simulator.name: DLR Mars UV simulator
dlr_mars_uv_simulator.provides: Lamp-based simulator of the incident Martian surface UV spectrum (published description; abstract-level record only).

aarhus_awts2.name: Aarhus Wind Tunnel II (AWTS II), Planetary Environment Facility
aarhus_awts2.provides: Pressure 1 bar to 10⁻³ mbar, CO₂/N₂/He gas mixes, sample temperature control to −170 °C, wind to 18 m/s; Mars dust/aeolian studies.

cu_impact_dusty_plasma.name: University of Colorado IMPACT Dusty Plasma Laboratory
cu_impact_dusty_plasma.operator: IMPACT (formerly CCLDAS), University of Colorado Boulder
cu_impact_dusty_plasma.provides: Vacuum chambers (51 cm and 60 cm 'KEG') for dusty-plasma, dust charging and photoelectron-sheath experiments relevant to lunar dust.

nasa_ames_lunar_lab.name: NASA Ames Lunar Lab and Regolith Testbeds
nasa_ames_lunar_lab.provides: Simulant-filled testbeds with low-angle lighting reproducing south-polar long shadows and high-contrast glare for rover vision tests.

esa_dlr_luna.name: ESA–DLR LUNA analogue facility
esa_dlr_luna.provides: ~700 m² hall with ~900 t of basalt-derived regolith simulant, lighting and a deep area for drilling/sampling; inaugurated 25 Sep 2024.

exolith_lhs1.name: Exolith Lab LHS-1 Lunar Highlands Simulant
exolith_lhs1.provides: High-fidelity lunar highlands regolith simulant (south pole is highland terrain).

exolith_mgs1.name: Exolith Lab MGS-1 Mars Global Simulant
exolith_mgs1.provides: Mineralogy-based Mars global regolith simulant; used for ISRU/water-extraction tests.

nasa_nu_lht.name: NASA NU-LHT lunar highlands simulant
nasa_nu_lht.provides: Highlands simulant made from Stillwater norite, anorthosite and harzburgite plus Twin Sisters dunite.
